# requires: logging
#
# What one encoded record looks like, and nothing about what is in it. A
# message, a host name and an instant belong to one machine, so every assertion
# here is about the shape of a line -- which fields are present, how a number is
# spelled, how wide a timestamp is. Two implementations that disagree about any
# of that disagree about the format itself, which is the only thing this layer
# asks several languages to share.
#
# The three `level` steps are the reason the scale is numeric. A binding whose
# language has a level this one does not name must land between landmarks and
# say so, rather than rounding to the nearer name and losing the distinction the
# other language was making.
level 8
level 12
level 2
record R 0
attr R bytes 328597408
group R http status 200
read R bytes
read R http.status
keys R
encode R

# expect 1: ok name=ERROR [LOG-R4]
# expect 2: ok name=ERROR+4 [LOG-R4]
# expect 3: ok name=INFO+2 [LOG-R4]
# expect 7: ok type=string value=328597408 [LOG-R5]
# expect 8: ok type=string value=200 [LOG-R6]
# expect 9: ok bytes,http.status [LOG-R6]
# expect 10: ok schema=1 level=0 frac=6 zone=Z lines=1 end=lf [LOG-R1] [LOG-R2] [LOG-R3] [LOG-R7]
